scenarios.title: Office Fire
scenarios.description: Recognise a fire warning, select a safe route, and reach the assembly point.
scenarios.environment: An office floor with a fire alarm, marked exits, smoke cues and a designated assembly point.
scenarios.learningNote: This is a simplified learning simulation, not a substitute for your premises' fire plan or professional training.

decisions.title: You notice smoke and hear the fire alarm.
decisions.hint: Leave promptly using the safe route in the premises plan. Do not delay for possessions or to investigate.

options.label: Raise the alarm if needed and begin evacuating by a safe marked route
options.feedback: Good decision: prioritise evacuation and follow the building's emergency plan.

options.label: Go toward the smoke to find the source
options.feedback: Investigating can delay escape and expose you to smoke. Prioritise the evacuation procedure.

options.label: Collect your bag and laptop first
options.feedback: Do not delay evacuation to collect possessions.

decisions.title: You have lost time while the alarm is active.
decisions.prompt: What is the safest next action?
decisions.hint: Do not attempt to investigate or recover belongings. Follow the evacuation plan.

options.label: Stop the task and leave by a safe marked route
options.feedback: Correct: evacuate without further delay.

options.label: Check nearby rooms before leaving
options.feedback: Do not search rooms unless this is specifically part of your trained role and safe to do so.

decisions.title: You see an exit sign and a lift lobby.
decisions.hint: Use a suitable, safe escape route. Ordinary lifts should not be used during a fire unless specifically designated by the building's evacuation plan.

options.label: Follow the nearest safe marked emergency exit
options.feedback: Correct: use a safe escape route identified by the premises plan.

options.label: Take the ordinary passenger lift
options.feedback: Ordinary lifts are generally not a fire escape route. Follow the building's plan.

options.label: Take the shortest route even though it is filled with smoke
options.feedback: Do not deliberately enter a smoke-filled route. Seek a safe alternative according to the emergency plan.

decisions.title: Smoke is gathering along one corridor.
decisions.prompt: The direct corridor is smoky. What should you do?
decisions.hint: Avoid entering dense smoke. Use a safe alternative route if one is available and identified by the emergency plan.

options.label: Avoid the smoky corridor and use a known safe alternative route
options.feedback: Correct: do not knowingly move into a smoke-filled escape route.

options.label: Continue through the smoke because it is shorter
options.feedback: Smoke can quickly make escape unsafe. Do not choose a route known to be smoke-filled.

options.label: Pause in a safe place and follow the site's emergency instructions
options.feedback: Follow the site plan and instructions from trained personnel; do not enter a visibly unsafe route.

decisions.title: A closed door is between you and another route.
decisions.prompt: You suspect the door may be hot. What is the better decision?
decisions.hint: Do not open a door you suspect is hot or leads into smoke or fire. Seek a safe alternative and follow the site procedure.

options.label: Do not open it; choose another safe route or follow the site's trapped-person procedure
options.feedback: Correct: avoid opening a door suspected to be hot or unsafe.

options.label: Open it quickly and see what is on the other side
options.feedback: Opening a potentially hot or smoke-exposed door can expose you to danger.

options.label: Wait beside the door without telling anyone
options.feedback: Move to the safest available option and communicate your situation according to the emergency plan.

decisions.title: You have reached the designated assembly point.
decisions.prompt: What should happen after you get outside?
decisions.hint: Stay at the assembly point, report missing people to the responsible person and do not re-enter.

options.label: Remain at the assembly point and report any known missing person
options.feedback: Correct: help account for occupants and keep clear of emergency-service access.

options.label: Go back inside to find a colleague
options.feedback: Never re-enter a fire-affected building. Tell the fire service or responsible person who may be missing.

options.label: Leave without checking in with the responsible person
options.feedback: Follow the site's assembly and headcount process so that missing people can be identified.

decisions.title: A colleague who may need evacuation assistance has not arrived.
decisions.hint: Tell the fire marshal or emergency services where the person was last seen. Follow the site's assisted-evacuation plan.

options.label: Tell the responsible marshal or emergency services and share the last known location
options.feedback: Correct: pass on information and let trained responders act under the evacuation plan.

options.label: Re-enter and search for the colleague yourself
options.feedback: Do not re-enter. Give the information to trained responders.

options.label: Assume someone else will report it
options.feedback: Report relevant information promptly to the responsible person.

scenarios.title: Blocked Exit
scenarios.description: Respond to an escape route that is obstructed or affected by fire or smoke.
scenarios.environment: An office corridor where the usual exit is blocked; alternative exits and an assembly point are indicated.
scenarios.learningNote: Route choices must be checked against the real building emergency plan.

decisions.title: Your usual exit is blocked by smoke and debris.
decisions.hint: Do not try to pass a route that is visibly unsafe. Look for a safe marked alternative from the premises plan.

options.label: Avoid the blocked route and use a safe, marked alternative
options.feedback: Correct: avoid the unsafe exit and follow the evacuation plan.

options.label: Push through the smoke and debris
options.feedback: Do not enter a route known to be unsafe.

options.label: Try to remove the blockage before evacuating
options.feedback: Do not delay or put yourself at risk trying to clear a hazardous escape route.

decisions.title: The alarm is sounding, but some nearby people may not have noticed.
decisions.prompt: What is appropriate if it is safe to do so?
decisions.hint: Raise the alarm and alert people nearby while continuing to evacuate; do not delay or enter danger.

options.label: Raise/confirm the alarm, alert nearby people if safe, and evacuate
options.feedback: Correct: warning others is appropriate when it does not expose you to additional danger.

options.label: Search the whole floor before leaving
options.feedback: Do not delay evacuation to conduct a search unless you have a trained role and the procedure allows it safely.

options.label: Wait indefinitely for someone else to make a decision
options.feedback: Follow the alarm and established evacuation procedure promptly.

decisions.title: Two possible routes are shown on the evacuation sign.
decisions.hint: Choose a route that is known to be safe and available, following the premises plan and instructions from trained staff.

options.label: Use the available marked route confirmed to be safe
options.feedback: Correct: select a safe available exit, not simply the shortest route.

options.label: Use the shortest route even though it is reported unsafe
options.feedback: Do not choose a known unsafe route because it is shorter.

options.label: Take the normal lift to another floor
options.feedback: Use the fire evacuation plan; ordinary lifts are generally unsuitable during a fire.

decisions.title: Someone asks you to go back for their bag.
decisions.hint: Personal belongings should not delay evacuation.

options.label: Ask them to leave it and continue evacuating
options.feedback: Correct: belongings are not worth delaying escape.

options.label: Go back together to collect it
options.feedback: Do not re-enter or delay evacuation to collect property.

options.label: Stay to argue about the bag
options.feedback: Keep moving toward safety and communicate calmly if it is safe to do so.

decisions.title: You are outside the building.
decisions.hint: Use the designated assembly point and keep clear of emergency access routes.

options.label: Go to the designated assembly point and check in
options.feedback: Correct: the assembly point supports an orderly headcount.

options.label: Wait directly at the entrance where fire crews need access
options.feedback: Keep clear of access routes and follow assembly-point instructions.

options.label: Leave without reporting to anyone
options.feedback: Follow site headcount procedures and report any missing people.

decisions.title: A person may still be inside near the blocked exit.
decisions.hint: Give responders the person's last known location and any relevant details. Do not re-enter.

options.label: Tell the marshal or fire service what you know
options.feedback: Correct: report information to trained responders and stay out of the building.

options.label: Go back through the blocked exit to check
options.feedback: Never re-enter a fire-affected building to search.

options.label: Say nothing because you are not certain
options.feedback: Share uncertainty honestly; responders can assess the information.

scenarios.title: Smoke-Filled Stairwell
scenarios.description: Choose safe actions when smoke affects a stairwell or the usual evacuation route.
scenarios.environment: A multi-storey building where smoke is visible in a stairwell and a designated safe area or alternative route may be available.
scenarios.learningNote: The correct action depends on the premises plan, building design, and emergency-service instructions.

decisions.title: You reach a stairwell and see smoke inside it.
decisions.hint: Do not deliberately enter a smoke-filled stairwell. Follow the site's emergency plan and seek a safe alternative.

options.label: Avoid entering the smoke-filled stairwell and follow the safe alternative in the plan
options.feedback: Correct: do not enter a route known to be smoke-filled.

options.label: Enter and hurry down through the smoke
options.feedback: Smoke can rapidly make the route untenable. Do not choose a known unsafe route.

options.label: Use the ordinary lift instead
options.feedback: Follow the premises fire plan; normal passenger lifts are generally not evacuation routes in a fire.

decisions.title: No immediately safe route is apparent.
decisions.prompt: What is a safer next step?
decisions.hint: Follow the building's trapped-person procedure. Depending on the plan, this may mean reaching a designated refuge/safe room, closing the door, and contacting emergency services.

options.label: Follow the building's procedure for being unable to evacuate and contact emergency services
options.feedback: Correct: use the site's procedure and communicate your location rather than entering smoke.

options.label: Jump from a window to escape
options.feedback: Do not jump. Move to a safer location if possible and call for help.

options.label: Hide without alerting anyone
options.feedback: Communicate your location to emergency services or responsible personnel when safe to do so.

decisions.title: You can make an emergency call or send an alert.
decisions.hint: Give your exact location, floor/room if known, the blocked or smoky route, and any immediate assistance needs.

options.label: Contact emergency services and give your location and situation
options.feedback: Correct: clear location information helps responders find you.

options.label: Assume someone else will have called
options.feedback: Do not assume. Contact emergency services if you can safely do so and follow local procedures.

options.label: Wait until the situation is worse before calling
options.feedback: Seek help promptly when you cannot safely evacuate.

decisions.title: You have reached a room designated by the site's emergency plan.
decisions.prompt: What should you do while awaiting assistance?
decisions.hint: Follow the site's emergency procedure and instructions from emergency services. Keep the door closed if the procedure calls for it.

options.label: Follow the site's procedure, keep the location known, and follow dispatcher instructions
options.feedback: Correct: follow the established plan and keep communicating with responders.

options.label: Repeatedly open the door to check the corridor
options.feedback: Avoid exposing yourself to smoke; follow the emergency plan and responder instructions.

options.label: Move through an unknown smoky route without checking
options.feedback: Do not enter a route known or suspected to be unsafe.

decisions.title: You hear people outside and consider leaving through the window.
decisions.hint: Do not jump. Follow the building's procedure and instructions from emergency services.

options.label: Do not jump; remain in the safest available place and signal your location
options.feedback: Correct: communicate your location and wait for safe assistance if no safe route is available.

options.label: Jump to the ground
options.feedback: Jumping can cause serious injury. Do not jump; seek help.

options.label: Climb out without knowing the drop or conditions
options.feedback: Do not attempt a dangerous improvised exit. Follow the emergency plan and responders.

decisions.title: Emergency responders are coordinating the evacuation.
decisions.hint: Follow the official instructions and remain where responders can locate you unless they direct otherwise.

options.label: Follow responder instructions and keep others informed if safe
options.feedback: Correct: follow emergency-service instructions.

options.label: Leave the safe location without telling responders
options.feedback: Do not move into an unsafe route or lose contact with responders without a safe plan.

options.label: Go back into the building after reaching safety
options.feedback: Never re-enter a fire-affected building.
